research.abstract: Polygonatum zanlanscianense Pamp. is a perennial herb (Asparagaceae) endemic to China, whose rhizomes are used in folk medicine as a substitute for Polygonati Rhizoma. Although its plastome has been reported, the mitogenome remained uncharacterized. Here, we assembled and annotated the complete linear mitogenome of P. zanlanscianense and analysed its gene repertoire, codon usage, repeats, RNA editing sites, MTPTs, synteny, phylogeny and Ka/Ks. The 689,491-bp mitogenome (GC 46.23%) encodes 56 genes: 36 PCGs, three rRNA genes and 17 tRNA genes. Codon usage is biased toward A/U-ending codons. We identified 68 SSRs, 25 tandem repeats, 1366 dispersed repeat pairs, 585 predicted C-to-U editing sites concentrated at the first and second codon positions, and 30 MTPT fragments accounting for 2.24% of the mitogenome. Phylogenetic analysis placed P. zanlanscianense as sister to Polygonatum kingianum Collett & Hemsl. Median Ka/Ks was below 1 for 33 of the 35 genes analysed; although rpl5 and ccmB showed elevated ratios, branch-site tests did not support positive selection. This first mitogenome of P. zanlanscianense provides genomic resources for comparative genomic, phylogenetic and medicinal studies in Polygonatum.

Executed end-to-end via autonomous Native Rust bio-suite-supervisor optimization across 32 candidate RuNIE chains (total runtime 753.88 s; B = 1,000 UFBoot; 25,000 MCMC generations with 20% burn-in), RY3 purine/pyrimidine recoding under GTR+F+R4 reduces Blattodea/Isoptera compositional heterogeneity by 90.2% (RCFV = 0.0032 vs. 0.0326, ln L = -421,583.88), dating Root Blattodea/Isoptera to 238.4 Ma, Crown Isoptera to 148.8 Ma, Crown Neoisoptera to 98.6 Ma, and Crown Higher Termitidae to 54.2 Ma. Native Rust quartet multispecies coalescent inference (runie-quartet-coalescent across 18 gene trees and 11,436,768 quartets in 45.39 ms) recovers 8,910,008 satisfied quartets (normalized Q = 0.7791, mean LPP = 0.8386) while ABBA-BABA tests quantify secondary-contact allele sharing between invasive Coptotermes formosanus and C. gestroi. research.abstract: Phylogenomic Divergence and Post-K–Pg Adaptive Radiation Across Mammalia Under FreeRate, Quartet Coalescent, and Relaxed-Clock Models Resolving whether placental mammals diversified tens of millions of years before or immediately after the 66.02 Ma Cretaceous–Paleogene (K–Pg) mass extinction has long been confounded by third-codon compositional drift, body-mass substitution-rate allometry, untranslated mRNA UTR alignment overhangs, and asymmetric supermatrix missing data. Here we execute a multi-regime RuNIE and bio-suite-supervisor phylogenomic, quartet coalescent, relaxed molecular-clock, and codon selection synthesis across complete mammalian, sauropsid, and lissamphibian outgroup mitogenomes alongside matched nuclear coding loci, benchmarking Native Rust bio-suite operators against *MAFFT, *IQ-TREE with *LSD2, *ASTRAL, and *PAML codeml. Forensic alignment and calibration auditing reveals why our initial uncalibrated supermatrix inflated Crown Primates to 161.4 Ma (+91.9 Myr error) and Crown Placentalia to 184.8 Ma (+90.8 Myr error): aligning full-length RefSeq mRNAs retained 56.03% UTR overhang gaps across 36,010 columns while concatenating 13 nuclear taxa onto 64 mitogenomes padded 51 mitogenome-only species with 71.1%–72.4% missing data and extrapolated saturated strepsirrhine/tarsiiform terminal branches from a single outgroup date. Stripping UTR overhangs down to a reading-frame-locked 8,874-bp (2,958-codon) Nuclear CDS Exon Supermatrix (2.71% gaps) and a conserved 16,035-bp 37-gene mitogenome core (1.11% gaps) with RY3 recoding and multi-stratum calibration restores Crown Mammalia to 184.6 Ma (95% HPD: 158.0–212.0 Ma), Crown Theria to 161.5 Ma, Crown Placentalia to 94.0 Ma (79.9–109.4 Ma), Crown Primates to 69.5 Ma (55.9–82.2 Ma), and Crown Cetartiodactyla to 61.3 Ma (50.0–73.3 Ma), while the uncalibrated nuclear CDS clock spontaneously recovers the Long-Fuse model (Crown Placentalia 78.9 Ma; post-K–Pg Chiroptera 55.0 Ma and Cetartiodactyla 44.9 Ma). research.abstract: Abstract Eliminating lifelong immunosuppression can make islet transplantation a durable alternative to insulin therapy for type 1 diabetes. As short-course tolerogenic regimens are developed to replace lifelong immunosuppression, it is critical to test their robustness against perturbations such as hospital-acquired infections, which transplant recipients routinely encounter. Herein, we investigated whether rapamycin-loaded polymersomes (rPS), a subcutaneous nanotherapy that induces long-term murine islet allograft survival, can preserve host defenses in a Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) skin infection, and whether the resulting immune response from this distal infection relative to graft location erodes rPS-induced tolerance. rPS maintained neutrophil antibacterial activity despite inhibiting oxidative mechanisms in vitro , and rPS-treated mice demonstrated normal recovery following MRSA challenge. However, MRSA skin infection caused a decline of ∼43% in recipient survival for rPS-treated mice, despite surviving recipients retaining glucose-stimulated insulin responsiveness. This erosion of allograft acceptance coincided with a burst of IL-6 within 24h of the infection followed by elevated TNF-□ and neutrophilia at 13 days post-infection. Combining rPS with a single dose of methylprednisolone reduced IL-6 and TNF-α without altering neutrophilia, nearly doubling survival among infected recipients to 80%. Our findings demonstrate that partial dampening of inflammatory insults can restore superior islet allograft acceptance following perioperative infection.

research.abstract: Small lytic phages of the ssRNA Leviviricetes and ssDNA Microviricetes achieve host lysis by expression of a single protein, designated as an Sgl protein. Four ssRNA Sgls have been shown to inhibit steps in peptidoglycan biosynthesis: three target MurJ, the Lipid II flippase, and one targets MurA, the committed step of the pathway. A fifth Sgl, the E protein of the canonical ssDNA microvirus {varphi}X174, inhibits MraY, which catalyzes the synthesis of the first lipid-linked intermediate. This inhibition requires SlyD, a cytoplasmic FKBP-type peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase. The Sgl of the Caulobacter ssRNA phage {varphi}Cb5 (Cebevirus halophobicum) has not been characterized. Here, we present physiological evidence that Sgl{varphi}Cb5 targets MraY. Moreover, we show that, despite the absence of detectable sequence similarity, Sgl{varphi}Cb5 shares several features with the {varphi}X174 E protein, including the distribution of hydrophobic and charged residues, a proposed N-out, C-in membrane topology, and retention of lytic activity in an Sgl{varphi}Cb5 -LacZ fusion. Furthermore, expression of the Caulobacter cytoplasmic FKBP-type peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase CC2799 enhances Sgl{varphi}Cb5 -mediated lysis in E. coli. These parallels between Sgl function in a DNA phage and an RNA phage either represent remarkably consonant convergent evolution or some evolutionary cross-over event for which there is currently no precedent.

research.abstract: Abstract Dengue viruses 1-4 (DENV1-4) mostly circulate in endemic cycles involving humans and Aedes mosquitoes. However, rare dengue outbreaks originate from non-human primates. These spillovers are caused by sylvatic virus genotypes that are closely related to endemic strains of the same serotype, but some are caused by strains that fall between the four canonical serotypes on phylogenetic trees. It is not clear whether these genotypic differences are reflected in corresponding antigenic differences. Here, we characterized the antigenic features of QML-22, a divergent strain most closely related to DENV2. On an antigenic map, QML-22 clustered with other globally representative DENV2 strains. QML-22 was not as well neutralized by antisera raised against endemic DENV2 and was better neutralized by antisera from DENV1, 3, and 4 infections than other strains of DENV2. QML-22 had a cluster of distinct amino acid residues in domain I of the envelope (E) protein, with only scattered point mutations elsewhere in the envelope. A potently neutralizing anti-DENV2 antibody that targets this site in domain I of the E protein, 3F9, had >1000-fold lower neutralization of QML-22 than other endemic DENV2 strains, whereas other cross-reactive and DENV2-specific antibodies neutralized QML-22 and endemic strains to similar titers. When antisera from non-human primates infected with QML-22 or DENV2 reference strain S16803 were depleted with the heterologous virions, homologous neutralization was unaffected but heterologous neutralization was reduced, suggesting homologous neutralization was due to distinct epitopes. Evolutionary analyses showed the 3F9 epitope was under relaxed selection pressure compared to other neutralizing epitopes and that QML-22 had unique amino acids in this epitope relative to the likely common ancestor of all DENV2. These findings provide insight into the antigenic diversification of DENV and the possible evolution of new serotypes. Author summary Dengue viruses that are most distantly related to the four canonical serotypes originated in Borneo, suggesting this island is a possible site of early dengue virus diversification as well as continued evolution within an unidentified host species. Here, we find divergent strain QML-22 from Borneo shares many neutralizing epitopes with DENV2 but has a distinct epitope in an important region affecting potent DENV2 neutralization. This region of the virus also is variable within DENV2 and in other DENV serotypes, highlighting an important site of dengue virus diversification and evolution. The spillover threat of viruses like QML-22 remains unknown, but ecological changes in Borneo may increase this risk.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Climatic suitability is often used to infer historical range changes, yet whether suitable area predicts effective population size remains unexplored. We investigated this relationship in two Palearctic dragonflies with contrasting ecologies: Somatochlora arctica , a widespread peatland specialist, and S. meridionalis , a southern European species associated with shaded streams. We combined demographic reconstructions from individual reference genomes using the pairwise sequentially Markovian coalescent (PSMC), maximum entropy (MaxEnt) species distribution models projected across six paleoclimatic intervals spanning approximately 3.3 million years, and ancestral state reconstructions of peatland specialization. Predicted suitable area was consistently greater for S. arctica , reaching its greatest extent during the Last Glacial Maximum. However, its inferred effective population size was smaller than that of S. meridionalis for most of the last ∼275,000 years. Ancestral reconstructions placed the most probable gain of peatland specialization in the S. arctica lineage (Clade I) during the late Miocene, with a median age of 9.4 million years, predating the modeled climatic intervals. These findings indicate a decoupling of climatic suitability and demographic history. Patchy breeding habitat, population structure, and the isolated Scottish origin of the sampled S. arctica may contribute to this mismatch. Combining genomic, ecological, and phylogenetic approaches provides complementary insights into historical biogeography and highlights the limitations of interpreting suitable climate as available breeding habitat or using individual genomes to characterize species-wide demographic histories.

research.abstract: Purpose Molecular diagnostic tests and sputum-based assays are common techniques for the initial evaluation of tuberculosis (TB). However, given their limitations in certain clinical contexts, efforts have been made to develop other diagnostic markers. This review evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a three-gene host-response test (TB score) for the diagnosis of TB. Methods We performed systematic searches in seven databases until July 2026. We included observational studies evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of the TB score to diagnosis of TB across different clinical contexts. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Meta-analysis was performed using the logit function, and GRADE was employed to assess certainty of evidence (CoE). Results Twenty-eight studies were included. For distinguishing pulmonary TB from other respiratory diseases, the TB score showed a pooled sensitivity and specificity of 0.80 (95% CI: 0.73-0.84) and 0.72 (95% CI: 0.64-0.78), respectively, with an AUC of 0.82. When comparing pulmonary TB to healthy controls, sensitivity was 0.75 and specificity was 0.86, with an AUC of 0.87. Performance was lower for meningeal tuberculosis (sensitivity 0.58; specificity 0.67) and for distinguishing active from latent TB (sensitivity 0.73; specificity 0.76). Risk of bias was generally low. The CoE for most outcomes was very low. Conclusion The TB score shows moderate diagnostic accuracy for pulmonary TB, with pooled sensitivity below the WHO TPP minimum for a standalone triage test. High heterogeneity and very low CoE limit confidence in these findings. Its potential role as a complementary tool remains investigational and requires validation in prospective studies.

items.title: Becoming mega-diverse: integrative phylogenomics reveals heterogeneous diversification at high rate in Astragalus (Fabaceae)

research.abstract: Abstract Background Understanding why species diversity is so unevenly distributed across the Tree of Life remains a central question in evolutionary biology. With more than 3,100 species, Astragalus (Fabaceae) is the largest genus of flowering plants and provides an exceptional system for investigating the factors of angiosperm megadiversity. However, despite recent phylogenomic advances, uncertainties in phylogenetic relationships and limited integration of available genomic resources have hindered comprehensive evolutionary analyses. Methods Here, we reconstruct the most comprehensive phylogenomic framework for Astragalus to date by integrating newly generated target enrichment data for 127 samples, representing 123 Astragalus taxa, with previously published target-capture, transcriptomic, and genome-skimming datasets. The resulting phylogeny includes 407 accessions representing 379 Astragalus species and provides a robust backbone for investigating diversification and genome evolution across the genus. Using a representative reduced dataset, we estimated divergence times, quantified diversification-rate heterogeneity, examined phylogenomic conflict, and evaluated evidence for whole-genome duplication (WGD). Key Results Our analyses recover a largely stable backbone for the deeper Astragalus lineages while revealing extensive gene-tree discordance concentrated in younger radiations, consistent with incomplete lineage sorting and reticulate evolution during rapid Miocene diversification. Diversification analyses indicate sustained lineage accumulation over approximately 18 million years, with pronounced rate shifts in several clades, particularly within the species-rich Neo-Astragalus lineage. Comparisons of alternative WGD scenarios across the phylogeny provided strongest support for a WGD at the crown node of Neo-Astragalus, with alternative placements receiving weaker support. This result provides a testable hypothesis for a WGD near the origin of the most rapidly diversifying lineage in the genus, although chromosome-scale genomic data will be required to confirm its occurrence and timing. Conclusions Together, our results indicate that the extraordinary diversity of Astragalus did not arise from a single evolutionary innovation or explosive radiation. Instead, megadiversity arose through the long-term interplay of sustained diversification, reticulate evolution, genome restructuring, and likely environmental change coupled with ecological adaptation. Beyond providing the most comprehensive phylogenomic hypothesis for the genus, this study establishes a robust framework for future investigations of biogeography, trait evolution, genome evolution, and the processes underlying exceptional species richness in flowering plants.

items.title: Unsupervised Clustering Enables Cohort-Specific Variant Recalibration in Crops
items.summary: Trait discovery in crops require reliable marker datasets, yet variant discovery remains constrained by the lack of standardised, high-confidence reference resources. research.abstract: Abstract Trait discovery in crops require reliable marker datasets, yet variant discovery remains constrained by the lack of standardised, high-confidence reference resources. Publicly available plant genomic resources often rely on outdated reference genomes, heterogenous pipelines, and generic variant hard-filtering thresholds derived from human studies. Consequently, applying the Genome Analysis Toolkit (GATK) Best Practices framework, particularly machine learning-based variant quality score recalibration (VQSR), remains challenging in crops lacking suitable training resources. Here, we present an unsupervised approach for variant quality assessment and generating cohort-specific training resources, enabling integration of VQSR into established GATK workflows without predefined high-confidence training variant sets. Using Brassica napus as a model, we use the Illumina 60k Brassica SNP array to establish a reference-specific truth set for base quality score recalibration (BQSR) and independent benchmarking. Gaussian mixture model (GMM)-based clustering of multidimensional variant annotation profiles identifies high-, intermediate-, and low-quality variant classes, which provide flexible training resources without requiring labelled training data. We further validate the approach in diploid Brassica oleracea and hexaploid wheat ( Triticum aestivum ), representing contrasting population characteristics and genome architectures. Across all three species, GMM-based clustering consistently identifies informative quality classes and enables cohort-specific recalibration of both SNPs and insertion-deletions (INDELs). Comparison with conventional hard filtering reveals discordant pass/fail classifications for up to 46.4% of SNPs and 37.8% of INDELs across evaluated cohorts, demonstrating that the approaches capture distinct aspects of variant quality. Our results establish unsupervised variant classification as transferable strategy for generating cohort-specific VQSR resources, extending established GATK workflows to crops lacking comprehensive genomic resources.

research.abstract: Streptococcus pyogenes causes diseases ranging from mild pharyngitis to life-threatening invasive infection, yet the genomic determinants of this variation remain poorly understood. We analyzed 1,863 publicly available genomes, whose pangenome comprises 6,568 genes (1,392 core and soft-core, 656 shell, and 4,520 cloud), and grouped isolates into 15 genetic groups with FastBAPS. Ten groups were monophyletic on the global phylogeny, and non-monophyly of the remaining five largely reflected the placement of isolates from group 12, which is dispersed across the tree. A GenomegaMap scan identified 163 of 3,147 genes with ω₀ > 1. These genes were depleted among core genes and enriched among cloud genes, a pattern consistent with positive selection on recently acquired genes but also with the retention of slightly deleterious variation in young genes. A putative IS transposase (K07497) was the most consistent functional enrichment signal, which led us to analyze insertion sequence (IS) elements directly. In group 12, complete IS copies within genomes were more often near-identical than in other groups (OR = 1.46), consistent with more recent IS activity, and genes with ω₀ > 1 were 2.9 times more likely than other accessory genes to lie within 5 kb of an IS element (8.8% vs. 3.0%; permutation p = 0.0006) after excluding IS-encoded genes. We did not detect this association in any other group, and most genes under selection were not IS-proximal.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE) species are common healthcare-associated pathogens that cause difficult-to-treat infections. Whole genome sequencing of patients has revealed a substantial burden of patient-to-patient VRE transmission in hospitals, with patients in intensive care units (ICUs) at particularly high risk of acquisition. However, few studies adequately characterize the pathways of VRE transmission between patients in acute care settings—a necessary step to identify current gaps in infection prevention practices. By harnessing genomic clustering analyses of whole genome sequences of VRE isolates from patients, environmental surfaces, and healthcare providers (HCP) in ICUs, we aim to reconstruct indirect pathways of pathogen movement to identify patterns of VRE spread and opportunities for transmission prevention. Methods and Findings We collected daily samples (N = 6848) from ICUs in two hospitals over 13 weeks from four main sampling sources: patients, HCP hands, patient rooms, and shared surfaces. Samples were cultured on selective media and sent for whole genome sequencing (WGS). We used genomic thresholds to identify clusters of related VRE isolates and distinguish unrelated isolates. VRE was detected in samples from 20 out of 322 unique occupant-stays (6.22%). VRE isolates were detected from all sampling sources except for shared surfaces. A total of 44 unique VRE isolates were identified, 43 Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) and one Enterococcus faecalis (VREf). Two distinct patterns of VREfm spread were observed: 1) an outbreak setting with observed patient-to-patient transmission and low VRE genomic heterogeneity, and 2) high VRE genomic heterogeneity and pathogen movement between occupant-stays facilitated by persistent HCP and environmental contamination, but no observed transmission events. VRE detection probabilities were not significantly different between occupant-stays in outbreak and non-outbreak settings (OR = 0.63, 95% CI (0.23, 1.83), p = 0.32). However, including VRE isolates from non-patient samples increased the number of occupant-stays with VRE detection from 6 to 20, a 3.3-fold increase, as compared to patient samples alone. Including non-patient samples also increased the number of VRE multi-isolate genomic clusters detected by 7-fold. Our findings are limited because sampling was primarily conducted in ICUs. Due to the combination of short ICU stay durations and imperfect test sensitivity, VRE transmission events may have been underdetected. Conclusions Our findings characterize the complex nature of VRE transmission pathways in ICU settings. Even without an ongoing outbreak, we found substantial evidence of VRE movement between occupant-stays, facilitated by a combination of HCP hands and environmental surfaces. This study highlights the importance of environmental sampling for understanding VRE transmission potential, which is likely to be underestimated using patient sampling alone. We recommend that future studies incorporate follow-up sampling after discharge to better understand the true burden of transmission.
